question: A and B can finish a piece of work in 15 days and 20 days, respectively. If A and B work on alternate days, how many days will it take to complete the work (A starts the work)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(15, 20) = 60 units.

Efficiency of A = 4 units/day, Efficiency of B = 3 units/day.

Work done in 2 days (1 cycle of A and B) = 4 + 3 = 7 units.

In 16 days (8 cycles), work done = 8 × 7 = 56 units.

Remaining 4 units are completed by A on the 17th day exactly in 1 day.

**∴ The correct answer is 17 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 15 days

Time taken by B = 20 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 15
 60
 4
 
 

 B
 20
 3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done by A on day 1 = 4 units

⇒ Work done by B on day 2 = 3 units

⇒ Total work done in 2 days = 4 + 3 = 7 units

⇒ Multiply by 8 to reach closest to total work: Work done in 16 days = 7 × 8 = 56 units

⇒ Remaining work = 60 − 56 = 4 units

⇒ On the 17th day, it is A's turn to work.

⇒ Time taken by A to complete remaining 4 units = 4 ÷ 4 = 1 day

⇒ Total days taken to finish the work = 16 + 1 = 17 days

**∴ The correct answer is 17 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Day Work

In alternate day problems, identify the total work done in one complete cycle of days, calculate the maximum full cycles possible without exceeding total work, and then manually track the remaining work day by day.

Pipes & Cisterns

Similar to the Time & Work concept, filling pipes have positive efficiency while emptying pipes (leaks) have negative efficiency.

Work & Wages

Wages are strictly distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each individual. If they work for the same number of days, the wages can directly be distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.
